target: RH cosmetic stud first; LH only after the RH method is checked
known_issue: uniform axial sampling does not preserve helical slope-break edges; repeated width/reflection modulation

parameter_policy.status: All remain estimated cosmetic values, not OEM facts.

construction_method: Use parameter domain u=theta/(2pi), v=(z-z0)/pitch-u, so constant-v edges follow each existing profile break helix.
Clip cells to finite axial start/end planes; share seam and cap vertices, refuse zero-area triangles.
Keep the same analytic radial profile; no new crest radius, bevel, wear, diameter, pitch or thread hand asserted.
Union the replacement stud with retained original rod and articulation ball; only the combined stem body is allowed to change.
Recompute intentional normals and physical UV on that single changed body, retaining all other nine source objects and exported primitive buffers.
checks: Compare old/new profile at samples; verify every profile-break curve represented by mesh edges.
Closed connected positive stud and final stem, zero exact-null source/export triangles, positive used UV areas.
Protect head, glass, coating, seal, washer, nut, all covers, pivots, motions, materials and images byte-for-byte where transport permits.
Verify actual source interfaces and combined head poses remain clear.
Read short whole and base-detail diffuse/specular previews before freezing final96.
unknowns: Exact RDC diameter, pitch, thread hand, profile class, mounting depth and mating fit.
Whether related product photos resolve a crest rounding radius; none is currently inferred.
